tagline: For small WooCommerce shops on PayPal: refunds, disputes and unpaid invoices in one conversation, and no money moves without the owner’s yes.
introNote: PayPal runs in mock mode in this video: demo data, not a PayPal account.

steps.text: If you run a small WooCommerce shop on PayPal, refunds, disputes and unpaid invoices sit in separate screens, and one wrong refund costs real money. Tillwise is a store agent you simply talk to. It shows you the numbers, and it moves money only after you confirm. In this demo, PayPal runs in mock mode, on demo data.
Money never moves on a guess. The refund is previewed first, and when the owner says go ahead, the host asks once more before the PayPal call is made.
Under the hood, every MCP tool call is visible: the preview, the confirmation, then the refund call to PayPal mock mode, and its audit row.

This is the Money Desk, built inside AG Studio. Built-in charts and grids sit next to three custom widgets: refund rate, who still owes us, and dispute deadlines. The rows come through our MCP server from the PayPal tools, here on the mock ledger.

Studio's AI panel runs on the GitHub Copilot SDK. The model reads a read-only refund anomaly tool, quotes its figures, and adds a chart of refunds per day by reason, so the damaged mug shipments stand out against the weeks before.
The Studio agent is read-only: it has no tool that moves money. Refunds happen only in the voice flow, after a preview and the owner’s yes.
Tillwise and PayPal. Talk to your shop, see your money, and stay in control of every refund.

outroSub: Talk to your shop, see your money, confirm every refund.
outroNote: PayPal ran in mock mode here: deterministic demo data, not a PayPal account. The Alexa+ experience simulator is an unofficial demo, not an Amazon product.
